question: Should internal requester consumption permanently satisfy descendant delivery even when the parent’s final outward send fails?
rationale: Delivery status controls user-visible retry, cleanup, persistence, and detached-task state, so choosing internal consumption as terminal proof requires an explicit lifecycle contract.

options.title: Separate consumption from delivery
options.body: Persist exact consumption metadata but keep descendant delivery retryable until the parent result reaches the approved durable outward-delivery boundary.

options.title: Accept internal consumption
options.body: Treat exact requester consumption as terminal delivery despite parent-send failure, with explicit contract documentation and live restart proof.

options.title: Use durable inbox design
options.body: Pause this branch and resolve consumed-but-not-user-delivered completions through the broader durable completion inbox or spool design.

recommendation.title: Separate consumption from delivery
recommendation.body: Persist exact consumption metadata but keep descendant delivery retryable until the parent result reaches the approved durable outward-delivery boundary.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history provides the strongest ownership signal across both subagent lifecycle and canonical detached-task state.
